question: Evaluate the determinant $\begin{vmatrix} \cos^2\theta & \cos\theta & 1 \\ \sin^2\theta & \sin\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$ and simplify your answer.
explanation:
Let $D = \begin{vmatrix} \cos^2\theta & \cos\theta & 1 \\ \sin^2\theta & \sin\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$.

Expand along the first row.

$D = \cos^2\theta \begin{vmatrix} \sin\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} - \cos\theta \begin{vmatrix} \sin^2\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} + 1 \begin{vmatrix} \sin^2\theta & \sin\theta \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$.

Compute minors.

$\begin{vmatrix} \sin\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \sin\theta - 1$.

$\begin{vmatrix} \sin^2\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \sin^2\theta - 1$.

$\begin{vmatrix} \sin^2\theta & \sin\theta \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \sin^2\theta - \sin\theta$.

Substitute back.

$D = \cos^2\theta(\sin\theta -1) - \cos\theta(\sin^2\theta -1) + (\sin^2\theta - \sin\theta)$.

Expand terms.

$= \cos^2\theta \sin\theta - \cos^2\theta - \cos\theta \sin^2\theta + \cos\theta + \sin^2\theta - \sin\theta$.

Group similar terms and simplify.

$= (\cos^2\theta \sin\theta - \cos\theta \sin^2\theta) + (-\cos^2\theta + \cos\theta) + (\sin^2\theta - \sin\theta)$.

Recognize common factors.

$\cos^2\theta \sin\theta - \cos\theta \sin^2\theta = \cos\theta \sin\theta(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)$.

After simplification the determinant becomes:

$(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)(1 + \cos\theta \sin\theta) - \cos2\theta$.
